version.changelog: Simplify the login instructions to the code flow (maton login prints a link; finish with maton login --code <CODE>), drop the API Key subsection, and pin the Maton CLI install to 0.4.0.

llm.summary: This is a clearly documented Outlook integration that can access and change mailbox, calendar, and contact data only through user-approved Maton authentication, with no hidden executable payload found.

dimensions.detail: Network access, OAuth, OS credential storage, and optional MATON_API_KEY usage are expected for Outlook API access and include clear handling guidance and least-privilege warnings.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Installation uses a pinned global Maton CLI package or Maton Homebrew tap, with optional pinned SDKs; this is disclosed and coherent with the API integration purpose.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Instructions repeatedly default to read/list operations, require explicit confirmation for writes, connection creation, hosted functions, triggers, destinations, and local --exec automation, and treat external data as untrusted.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: OAuth tokens, hosted functions, and triggers can persist beyond one session, but the artifact discloses this, scopes it to the user's Maton account, and requires user approval and cleanup guidance.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The skill's Outlook read, send, delete, calendar, contacts, hosted function, and trigger capabilities are sensitive but match the stated Microsoft Graph/Maton integration purpose.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Before installing, understand that this skill can read and modify Outlook email, folders, calendar events, and contacts through your authorized account. Use OAuth rather than long-lived API keys where possible, approve every write or automation explicitly, and be especially careful with triggers or destinations because they can create ongoing data flows.
